newsitem.title: ISRAEL: McDonald's claims victory in Israel kosher dispute.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's claims victory in Israel kosher dispute.

text.p: McDonald's Israeli franchise claimed a victory on Wednesday in a dispute with landlord Africa Israel Investments over whether a Tel Aviv restaurant would conform to Jewish dietary law.
But Africa Israel, one of Israel's largest property companies, insisted there was no battle at all.
Omri Padan, managing director of McDonald's Israel, said Africa Israel had agreed the restaurant slated to open in Africa Israel's new mall in north Tel Aviv would not be kosher.
Victorious in one battle, Padan said he was hoping Africa Israel would now consent to allowing the restarant to open on the Jewish Sabbath, which runs from Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.

"If they will (agree), there will be a degree of satisfaction here that at least in the Tel Aviv area individual freedom and the ability of people to use their free time as they choose will have been preserved," he told Israel Radio.
But an Africa Israel spokeswoman denied there was ever a disagreement between the two sides over the observance of dietary laws known as kashrut.
"There was no argument over the matter of kashrut ... the argument has been over the Sabbath," Anat Weiss told Reuters.
She pointed out that only two out of 40 McDonald's outlets in Israel were kosher.

Padan has emerged as a hero for Israelis worried about religious coercion after he locked horns over the McDonald's branch with Lev Leviev, who acquired Africa Israel earlier this year. Leviev, a religious Jew, said he aimed to make the company follow Jewish religious law wherever possible.
Africa Israel's new mall sits in the heart of Tel Aviv's overwhelmingly secular Ramat Aviv neighbourhood.

The issue of closing on the Sabbath is not in Padan's hands. Weiss said McDonald's lease says opening on the Sabbath depends on whether cinemas in the mall controlled by another company, Israel Theatres, would be open on the Sabbath.
"There is no signed contract yet with Israel Theatres," Weiss said.
